name: Arizona
nameStory: Most likely from the O'odham phrase 'ali shonak' - 'small spring' - picked up by the Spanish as 'Arizonac.' An entire desert state is named after a little spring, which tells you exactly what a small water source is worth out there.
capitalStory: Phoenix was named by a settler who looked at the abandoned canals of the Hohokam people and predicted a new city would rise from that dead civilization's ashes. He was right very literally: modern Phoenix still moves water along Hohokam canal routes.

majorFeatures.name: Grand Canyon
majorFeatures.note: 277 river miles long, up to a mile deep

majorFeatures.name: Colorado River
majorFeatures.note: Carved the canyon; forms the California border

majorFeatures.name: Sonoran Desert
majorFeatures.note: The only place saguaro cactus grows wild

majorFeatures.name: Painted Desert
majorFeatures.note: Banded badlands of red and purple rock

funFacts: The last of the contiguous 48 states admitted, on Valentine's Day 1912.
Arizona ignores Daylight Saving Time; it is hot enough without an extra hour of evening sun. The Navajo Nation inside it does observe DST.
It holds one corner of Four Corners, the only spot where four US states touch.
It has more land held by Native nations than any other state.
whyItMatters: Arizona depends on a Colorado River that no longer reliably reaches the sea. As Lake Mead drops, Arizona takes the first and deepest cuts, because of the junior water rights it accepted in 1968 to get its canal built.
